locator.section: 00 — Master Audit Blueprint > 1. Fuentes consideradas (parte 3/3)

chunks.summary:
### 1.2 Observaciones sobre las fuentes

- Los archivos antiguos hablan de una tesis en desarrollo. **Eso ya no es válido**.
- La tesis debe tratarse como: **completa, pendiente de sustentación**.
- Los archivos antiguos no deben usarse como calendario vigente.
- Las metas, proyectos y riesgos sí aportan contexto estratégico.
- Las fuentes salariales y legales del informe anterior no son suficientemente robustas.
- La lista de empresas del informe anterior es superficial: da ejemplos, pero no una base operativa de 100+ targets verificados.
- El Excel de cursos no fue integrado con suficiente rigor en el informe anterior.
- La investigación anterior mezcló español e inglés, afirmaciones fuertes y datos débiles.

---

| Cursos sin certificado | Usarlos como aprendizaje/skill proof, no como certificaciones formales. |

> **Technical Artist & Real-Time 3D Developer especializado en Unity, WebGL, C#, Blender, CAD-to-realtime optimization, interactive technical visualization y Python/AI-assisted production tooling.**

**Regla:** el nuevo plan 30/60/90 debe construirse desde la fecha actual y estado tesis completa.

| `deep-research-report` | Technical Artist / Real-Time 3D / XR / AI tooling | Amplio, pero falta jerarquía. |

### 5.4 Cursos y portfolio

| Deep report | Menciona Portugal/Alemania con afirmaciones legales | Debe verificarse con fuentes oficiales. |

**Regla:** el corto plazo es inglés + portfolio + remoto desde Colombia. Alemán/portugués son mediano plazo.

### 6.2 Diagnóstico inicial

locator.section: 00 — Master Audit Blueprint > 6. Inventario del Excel de cursos (parte 2/3)

chunks.summary:
El Excel demuestra acceso a formación amplia, pero también riesgo de dispersión. El problema no es falta de cursos; el problema es **convertir cursos en evidencia laboral**.

### 6.3 Regla de uso de cursos

Cada curso debe clasificarse así:

| Pregunta | Decisión |
|---|---|
| ¿Produce evidencia visible en portfolio? | Priorizar |

locator.section: 00 — Master Audit Blueprint > 12. Registro de riesgos estructurales (parte 1/2)

chunks.summary:
### 12.1 Riesgo de sobreespecialización incorrecta

**Problema:** apuntar solo a Game Technical Artist puede reducir probabilidad por competencia alta y menor entrada junior.

**Mitigación:** posicionar como Technical Artist / Real-Time 3D / Technical Visualization con ruta game como secundaria.

### 12.2 Riesgo de dispersión

**Problema:** cursos, VFX, Houdini, Human Portrait, ARA, FitApp, AI News, GitHub, portfolio, idiomas y job hunt compiten por atención.

**Mitigación:** matriz esfuerzo/impacto. Solo activos que soporten empleo en 3–6 meses.

### 12.3 Riesgo de sobreventa

**Problema:** presentar proyectos incompletos como producción o AI-assisted code como expert-level development.

**Mitigación:** wording honesto: prototype, research tool, AI-assisted, implemented/integrated/debugged by author.

### 12.4 Riesgo salarial

**Problema:** USD 6k/mes puede ser irrealista a corto plazo si se aplica como junior sin experiencia formal.

**Mitigación:** metas escalonadas:
- USD 1.5k: survival / mínimo inicial;
- USD 3k: contractor/nearshore viable;
- USD 6k: mid-level o nicho internacional a 12–24 meses.

### 12.5 Riesgo legal

locator.section: 00 — Master Audit Blueprint > 12. Registro de riesgos estructurales (parte 2/2)

chunks.summary:
**Problema:** asumir EU work authorization o manejo tributario incorrecto en Colombia.

**Mitigación:** fuentes oficiales, contador, wording conservador, contrato claro.

### 12.6 Riesgo de portfolio incompleto

**Problema:** aplicar sin caso de estudio visual puede reducir respuestas.

**Mitigación:** MVP mínimo: TwinSight case study + demo + screenshots + CV + LinkedIn.

### 12.7 Riesgo de análisis infinito

**Problema:** seguir investigando y no aplicar.

**Mitigación:** cada archivo debe producir decisiones y límites temporales.

locator.section: 02 — Market Role Fit and Positioning > 0. Propósito de esta sección (parte 1/2)

chunks.summary:
Este archivo define qué familias de roles debe perseguir Alexander en una búsqueda laboral internacional de 3–6 meses, idealmente remota desde Colombia, y qué rutas deben tratarse como secundarias, futuras o de contingencia.

La sección corrige la investigación previa en tres puntos:

1. **Separar familias de rol, job titles, industrias y keywords.** El informe anterior mezclaba `Technical Artist`, `Unity Developer`, `Digital Twin`, `CAD-to-realtime`, `WebGL`, `XR`, `AI Tools` y `Full-stack` como si fueran categorías equivalentes. No lo son.
2. **Priorizar por probabilidad, no solo por atractivo.** Un rol con salario alto puede ser poco útil si exige seniority, autorización laboral local, producción AAA, residencia en EE. UU./UE o experiencia formal no demostrada.
3. **Alinear cada rol con evidencia real.** TwinSight X500, ARA Framework, el retrato Blender y los proyectos secundarios no prueban lo mismo. Cada rol requiere un paquete de evidencia distinto.

### 4.1 Lectura de la matriz

La matriz no dice que el salario más alto esté en la prioridad 1. Dice que la mejor relación entre **evidencia actual + probabilidad + coherencia + upside** está en roles de 3D interactivo, visualización técnica y Unity/WebGL.

locator.section: 03 — Salary Benchmark and Remote-from-Colombia Feasibility > 1. Fuentes utilizadas y auditoría de calidad (parte 3/3)

chunks.summary:
No todas las fuentes tienen el mismo peso. Las fuentes de payroll y contratos reales son mejores que los agregadores de salarios. Los agregadores como ZipRecruiter son útiles para señales de mercado, pero mezclan ubicación, nivel, industria, tamaño de empresa, empleador local y trabajo remoto. Las guías de outsourcing suelen mostrar cifras desde la perspectiva de empresas que quieren contratar más barato, por lo que deben tratarse como **datos comerciales**, no como verdad neutral.

El informe anterior falló principalmente en tres puntos:

1. **Confundió salario local con salario accesible.** Un salario de EE. UU. no implica que una empresa pague ese monto a un contractor ubicado en Colombia.
2. **No separó gross de net.** USD 3,000/mes brutos como contractor no son USD 3,000/mes disponibles.
3. **Usó rangos demasiado amplios.** Para decidir estrategia, hace falta separar rol, seniority, modalidad contractual y restricción geográfica.

locator.section: 03 — Salary Benchmark and Remote-from-Colombia Feasibility > 2. Metodología de benchmark

chunks.summary:
### 2.1 Categorías de salario

| Categoría | Significado |
|---|---|
| Local employee | Nómina local en país específico |
| EOR employee | Empleado legal por intermediario |
| Direct contractor | Prestación de servicios / B2B |
| Marketplace contractor | Plataforma tipo Lemon.io |
| Freelance project | Proyecto puntual por alcance |
| Job-posting salary | Oferta o agregador de vacantes |
| Strategic estimate | Inferencia razonada |

### 2.2 Conversión mensual

Para efectos estratégicos:

```text
monthly gross = annual gross / 12
monthly contractor full-time = hourly rate × 160 hours
annual contractor full-time = hourly rate × 2,080 hours
```

Estas conversiones son aproximadas. Un contractor rara vez factura 160 horas productivas todos los meses durante 12 meses sin interrupción. Para modelar ingreso conservador, conviene usar 120–140 horas facturables/mes.

### 2.3 Confidence rating

| Rating | Uso |
|---|---|
| Alta | Payroll, fuente oficial, contrato real |
| Media | Marketplace, job posting amplio |
| Baja | Agregador, muestra pequeña, vendor |
| Muy baja | Snippet, SEO, dato no verificable |

locator.section: 03 — Salary Benchmark and Remote-from-Colombia Feasibility > 3. Conclusión ejecutiva salarial (parte 1/2)

chunks.summary:
Para Alexander, las rutas más coherentes con el objetivo económico son:

1. **Unity WebGL / Interactive 3D / Real-Time 3D contractor desde Colombia.** Es la ruta más alineada con TwinSight y con el objetivo de USD 1.5k–3k mensual en 3–6 meses.
2. **Technical Visualization / Digital Twin / Simulation.** Es la ruta con mayor upside a 12–24 meses, pero requiere empaquetar TwinSight como caso técnico serio y buscar empresas fuera de videojuegos.
3. **Unity Technical Artist — optimization/tools/runtime.** Es útil como etiqueta profesional, pero no debe confundirse con Game Technical Artist AAA.
4. **Python Automation / AI Tools.** Es ruta secundaria. Puede ayudar a monetizar ARA, pero no debe liderar la búsqueda inicial.
5. **3D Artist / Blender Generalist.** Debe quedar como fallback débil o complemento visual. No maximiza salario ni explota suficientemente TwinSight.

### 4.1 Real-Time 3D / Interactive 3D / Unity Developer

Esta familia es la base salarial más útil porque los datos de mercado para `Unity Developer` son más abundantes que para `Unity WebGL Technical Visualization Developer`.

#### Señales principales

- Howdy reporta que los salarios promedio de desarrolladores en LATAM en 2025 se ubican aproximadamente entre **USD 53k y USD 63k/año**, con Colombia alrededor de **USD 55,894/año** en su dataset de payroll. También reporta bandas LATAM de **USD 18k–28k junior**, **USD 35k–48k mid** y **USD 55k–70k senior**.[^howdy]
- Lemon.io reporta que un **Middle Unity Developer en Colombia** factura alrededor de **USD 27–35/h**, mientras que senior Unity developers en EE. UU. tienen mediana de **USD 57/h** y strong seniors en San Francisco llegan a **USD 72–89/h**.[^lemon-core]
- Qubit Labs reporta salarios mid-level Unity por país, con cifras como EE. UU. **USD 116,998**, Canadá **USD 140,000**, Alemania **USD 61,197**, UK **USD 58,709**, España **USD 58,719** y Brasil **USD 27,000**.[^qubit-country]

#### Matriz operativa

#### Lectura para Alexander

Esta es la ruta con mejor relación entre evidencia disponible y empleabilidad. TwinSight prueba Unity, C#, interacción 3D, UI técnica, optimización de assets y despliegue web. El riesgo es que muchas vacantes Unity están orientadas a juegos, mobile o VR. La búsqueda debe priorizar `Interactive 3D`, `Technical Visualization`, `WebGL`, `Simulation`, `Product Visualization` y `Unity Developer` fuera de game-only pipelines.

Los datos específicos de `Tools Developer` son escasos. La fuente de salario debe modelarse por proxies:

Esta ruta puede ser valiosa si ARA y scripts de pipeline se presentan correctamente. No obstante, para ganar entrevistas como `Tools Developer`, se necesita evidencia adicional:

- editor tools en Unity;
- automatización Blender/Python;
- pipeline CAD-to-realtime documentado;
- before/after de optimización;

- repositorio con README técnico.

### 7.1 Checklist básico

### 7.2 RUT

Colombia Move describe el RUT como el registro fiscal necesario para operar formalmente como independiente; incluye actividad económica CIIU y datos ante DIAN.[^colombiamove-rut]

Para Alexander, el RUT debe configurarse antes de facturar de forma sostenida a clientes extranjeros. La elección del CIIU debe validarse con contador. Posibles áreas: software development, consultoría, diseño, servicios digitales o actividades creativas/técnicas, según el modelo real de facturación.

### 7.3 Facturación electrónica

Colombia Move señala que si se factura a clientes colombianos y se superan ciertos ingresos, la factura electrónica DIAN-compliant es necesaria, y que DIAN ofrece una herramienta gratuita.[^colombiamove-invoice]

locator.section: 03 — Salary Benchmark and Remote-from-Colombia Feasibility > 7. Implicaciones administrativas en Colombia (parte 2/4)

chunks.summary:
Para clientes extranjeros, el tratamiento puede variar. La recomendación estratégica es no improvisar: configurar facturación electrónica y tener soporte documental de contratos y pagos desde el inicio.

### 7.4 Retención en la fuente

Para clientes colombianos, Colombia Move describe una retención típica del **10%** sobre honorarios profesionales y aclara que clientes extranjeros no aplican esa retención local.[^colombiamove-withholding]

Esto importa para comparar local vs internacional. Una oferta local de COP puede tener retenciones y flujo de caja distinto a una oferta extranjera en USD.

### 7.5 IVA / exportación de servicios

Colombia Move indica que el IVA general es **19%** y que muchos servicios profesionales son IVA-aplicables, pero también señala que ingresos por clientes extranjeros normalmente se tratan como exportación de servicios y suelen estar exentos, si se documenta correctamente.[^colombiamove-iva]

locator.section: 03 — Salary Benchmark and Remote-from-Colombia Feasibility > 7. Implicaciones administrativas en Colombia (parte 3/4)

chunks.summary:
Esta parte debe validarse con contador. No se debe asumir automáticamente `IVA 0%` para todo servicio remoto. La pregunta práctica no es solo “si el cliente está afuera”, sino si el servicio se utiliza exclusivamente en el exterior, cómo se factura, cómo se documenta y qué responsabilidades figuran en el RUT.

### 7.6 Seguridad social independiente

SIA Seguros resume que en 2026 todo independiente con ingresos iguales o superiores a 1 SMMLV debe cotizar a salud, pensión y ARL si aplica. También indica que para contratistas por prestación de servicios el IBC es **40% del valor mensual del contrato**, y para independientes por cuenta propia el Decreto 0379 de 2026 permite aplicar el 40% sobre ingreso neto después de costos en ciertos casos.[^sia-ibc]

Los porcentajes base reportados son:

| Concepto | Porcentaje |
|---|---:|
| Salud | 12.5% |
| Pensión | 16% |
| ARL nivel I | 0.522% |
| Base habitual | 40% ingreso |

La regla de costos netos no debe aplicarse sin asesoría. Para contrato de prestación de servicios, SIA indica explícitamente IBC sobre 40% del valor mensual del contrato.[^sia-contratistas]

chunks.summary:
The Deep Research output was useful as a directional draft, but it had quality problems that must be corrected before integration.

### 1.1 Valid findings to keep

The following points are directionally correct:

- **English is the highest short-term ROI language** for international remote roles.
- **German has low immediate ROI for remote-from-Colombia roles**, but high integration and mobility ROI if Germany becomes the relocation target.
- **Portuguese has medium strategic ROI** because of the expected Portuguese passport and possible Portugal residence, but it does not replace English for technical roles.
- **German should not displace English or portfolio work** in the first 3–6 months.
- **Portuguese is easier to acquire from Spanish than German**, so a functional B1/B2 path is realistic within 12–24 months if studied consistently.
- **Language certification is optional for most tech hiring**, but useful for immigration, academia, and credibility when the language claim is uncertain.

### 1.2 Weak or rejected parts

Several points in the Deep Research output were too broad or weakly sourced:

chunks.summary:
### Strongest signals

Non-certified courses from the Excel sheet are worth doing when they meet at least one condition:

### When a master’s becomes rational

A master’s becomes rational if at least three conditions are true:

1. Portuguese passport is obtained or nearly obtained.
2. Tuition drops due to EU status.
3. Program is in English or Spanish and directly tied to graphics/XR/simulation.
4. There is internship access.
5. There is relocation value.
6. Employment search has plateaued.
7. The program produces a portfolio/research project relevant to digital twins or simulation.

### When a master’s is irrational

A master’s is irrational if:

- it delays job applications;
- it is pursued to compensate for insecurity;
- it is unaffordable without income;
- it has weak industry placement;
- it is purely artistic and not technical;
- it does not create EU or network advantage.

### When it weakens the profile

- Goal is international employability in 3–6 months.
- Goal is USD 3k–6k/month income growth.
- Portfolio is not yet public.

- The PhD is used as an avoidance strategy.

### Decision

Do not pursue PhD now. Re-evaluate only after 2–3 years of industry experience or after a strong funded research opportunity appears.

locator.section: 06 — Education, Courses, Rebelway, Master’s and PhD Strategy > 18. How to present non-certified courses

chunks.summary:
### Do not write

- “Certified in Houdini” if no recognized certification exists.
- “Certified Technical Artist” if only a course was completed.
- Long lists of Udemy/Gnomon/Wingfox courses.
- “Mastered” unless there is public proof.

### Acceptable wording

- “Additional training in Houdini procedural workflows, Blender hard-surface asset production and realtime FX.”
- “Completed project-based training in Blender portrait production and technical asset workflows.”
- “Self-directed study supported by Rebelway, CG Cookie, Gnomon, Blender Bros and CG Circuit course material.”
- “Coursework used to produce portfolio artifacts: [project name].”

### Best practice

Attach each course cluster to an output:

- course → artifact;
- artifact → skill;
- skill → role;
- role → portfolio section.

locator.section: 06 — Education, Courses, Rebelway, Master’s and PhD Strategy > 19. Education risks

chunks.summary:
### Main risks

- Course hoarding.
- Certification chasing.
- Delaying applications.
- Fragmented identity.
- Over-indexing on Unreal while positioning as Unity.
- Becoming a generalist 3D artist instead of technical visualization developer.
- Spending months on CFX/character while the job target is interactive 3D.

### Control mechanisms

- No course without a deliverable.
- No more than one main course at a time.
- No long course before TwinSight is public.
- No certificate before portfolio MVP.
- No master before first job-search cycle.
- Monthly review: course output must become public evidence.

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 0. Purpose (parte 1/2)

chunks.summary:
This file defines the operating system for Alexander Woodcock Salomón’s international job search.

The goal is not to “apply more.” The goal is to run a controlled pipeline that converts the existing portfolio assets, especially TwinSight X500, into interviews, offers, contractor opportunities, and market feedback.

This system assumes the previous strategic decisions are already fixed:

- Primary target: Real-Time 3D / Interactive Technical Visualization / Unity WebGL.
- Secondary target: Unity Technical Artist focused on optimization, runtime systems, tools, shaders, and CAD-to-realtime workflows.
- Expansion target: Digital Twin / Simulation / XR / Industrial Visualization.
- Controlled secondary route: Tools / Python Automation / AI-assisted production tooling.
- Fallback routes: Full-stack and 3D generalist only when strategically useful.
- Current priority: remote from Colombia.
- Future mobility: Portuguese passport expected in approximately two years; Germany route possible through legal marriage and residence with German partner.

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 0. Purpose (parte 2/2)

chunks.summary:
This section is operational. It does not redefine the positioning. It translates the strategy into execution.

---

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 1. Core operating principle

chunks.summary:
The job search must be treated as a pipeline, not as scattered applications.

Every target should move through a controlled sequence:

```text
Target identified → Fit scored → Evidence selected → Application customized → Outreach sent → Follow-up → Interview → Test → Offer → Decision → Retrospective
```

The system must prevent four failure modes:

1. Applying to roles without enough fit.
2. Spending too much time customizing low-probability applications.
3. Over-positioning into roles where the evidence is weak.
4. Losing track of companies, conversations, follow-ups, and feedback.

The tracker is the source of operational truth.

---

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 2. Application categories

chunks.summary: All opportunities must be classified before applying.

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 2.1 Category A — High-fit targets

chunks.summary:
These are the highest-priority opportunities.

They match TwinSight directly and do not require major repositioning.

Examples:

- Interactive 3D Developer.
- Real-Time 3D Developer.
- Unity WebGL Developer.
- Technical Visualization Developer.
- Digital Twin Visualization Developer.
- Simulation Visualization Developer.
- Unity Developer for enterprise 3D.
- XR Developer for industrial or training applications.

A Category A opportunity should satisfy most of these conditions:

- Unity, WebGL, real-time 3D, simulation, digital twin, XR, or technical visualization is central to the role.
- A technical portfolio case study is relevant.
- TwinSight can be used as the primary proof.
- Remote, contractor, LATAM, or global work is plausible.
- The role does not require senior commercial experience as a hard gate.
- The company works in industrial, education, simulation, XR, training, product visualization, or enterprise 3D.

Application effort: high.

Customization level: strong.

Expected weekly volume: 5–8.

---

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 2.2 Category B — Adjacent targets

chunks.summary:
These are plausible but require adaptation.

Examples:

- Unity Technical Artist in games.
- Game Technical Artist.
- Shader Technical Artist.
- Tools Developer.
- Pipeline Developer.
- 3D product configurator developer.
- WebGL / Three.js Developer.
- Python Automation Developer.
- AI Tools Developer.

A Category B opportunity is valid when:

- The role is related to the portfolio but not a direct TwinSight match.
- ARA, Blender portrait, or shader work may support the application.
- Some missing skills exist, but the gap is not fatal.
- The application can be made credible without exaggeration.

Application effort: medium.

Customization level: moderate.

Expected weekly volume: 8–12.

---

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 2.3 Category C — Volume targets

chunks.summary:
These are lower-fit but useful for market testing, interview practice, or income fallback.

Examples:

- Junior Unity Developer.
- C# Developer with light Unity.
- Full-stack developer.
- Python automation support.
- Freelance web projects.
- 3D generalist roles.
- Simple contractor gigs.

A Category C opportunity is acceptable when:

- It can produce income quickly.
- It does not consume excessive customization time.
- It does not force a false professional identity.
- It can be applied to with a lighter version of the CV.

Application effort: low.

Customization level: minimal.

Expected weekly volume: 10–20.

---

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 2.4 Watchlist targets

chunks.summary:

Examples:

- Senior Technical Artist AAA.
- Senior Simulation Engineer.
- Digital Twin Architect.
- Research Engineer.
- Graphics Programmer.
- AI Engineer.
- EU-only roles requiring current EU work authorization.
- Germany-only roles requiring German language.

Watchlist targets should not consume active application time unless a specific opening unusually matches the profile.

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 3. Weekly application mix

chunks.summary:
A balanced weekly target should avoid both over-customization and indiscriminate spam.

Recommended baseline after the thesis defense:

| Category | Weekly target |
|---|---:|
| A | 5–8 |
| B | 8–12 |
| C | 10–20 |
| Speculative outreach | 10–15 |
| Recruiter contacts | 5–10 |

Total weekly outbound actions:

```text
Minimum controlled pace: 30 actions/week
Strong pace: 45–55 actions/week
Aggressive pace: 60–75 actions/week
```

An outbound action means one of the following:

- Submitted application.
- Recruiter message.
- Founder / technical lead outreach.
- Referral request.
- Follow-up.
- Portfolio feedback request.
- Community post with job-search relevance.

Do not count passive browsing as execution.

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 19.2 Monthly adjustment rules

chunks.summary:
After 30 days:

- Keep applying if response rate is acceptable.
- If no response, revise CV and portfolio front page.
- If roles reject due to authorization, shift toward LATAM contractor and global contractor platforms.
- If roles reject due to experience, increase project-based outreach.
- If roles reject due to skill gaps, schedule a focused sprint.

After 60 days:

- Double down on the top two responding role families.
- Stop applying to low-response categories.
- Use feedback to rewrite positioning.
- Increase direct outreach and referral attempts.

After 90 days:

- Reassess salary target.
- Consider contractor/freelance bridge work.
- Consider temporary fallback route if no traction.

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 21. Offer evaluation framework

chunks.summary:
Evaluate every offer using six dimensions.

| Dimension | Weight |
|---|---:|
| Net income | 30% |
| Role fit | 20% |
| Portfolio leverage | 15% |
| International leverage | 15% |
| Stability | 10% |
| Learning value | 10% |

Use this scoring:

```text
5 = excellent
4 = strong
3 = acceptable
2 = weak
1 = unacceptable
```

Any offer below 3/5 in both net income and role fit should be rejected unless there is an urgent financial need.

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 22. Gross-to-net tracking

chunks.summary:
Track compensation as gross and estimated net.

Required fields:

| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| Gross monthly | USD 3,000 |
| Payment currency | USD |
| Platform fee | 0–5% |
| Conversion spread | 0–3% |
| Social security reserve | Estimate |
| Tax reserve | Estimate |
| Net estimate | Conservative |

Do not compare offers only by gross salary.

A USD 3,000 contractor offer may be weaker than a lower employee offer if it has unstable payments, no benefits, and high compliance cost.

locator.section: Application System and Tracker > 34. Final operational recommendation

chunks.summary:

After 100 outbound actions, evaluate:

```text

2. Which market responds?
3. Which salary range responds?
4. Which project gets attention?
5. Which requirement blocks progress?
6. Which claim needs adjustment?
7. Which skill gap appears repeatedly?
```

locator.section: 13 — Interview, Negotiation and Offer-Risk Framework > 2. Source-quality audit of the Deep Research output (parte 1/2)

chunks.summary:
The Deep Research output was useful as a raw input, but not acceptable as a final section without correction.

### What was useful

- It identified common interview formats: screening, technical interview, take-home test, hiring-manager interview and offer stage.
- It surfaced representative Unity interview topics: GameObjects, components, `Update`, `FixedUpdate`, prefabs and colliders.
- It correctly separated employee and contractor negotiation issues.
- It highlighted red flags in remote offers.
- It connected salary anchoring to section 03 benchmarks.

### What required correction

- It repeated salary data that belongs primarily in section 03.
- It used some weak sources for interview patterns and red flags.
- It overstated some tax points, especially around IVA/exported services, which must be handled cautiously.
- It did not adequately separate role-family interview expectations.
- It did not provide a rigorous take-home test risk model.
- It did not give a structured offer-scoring model.
- It did not sufficiently address AI-assisted development disclosure.

### Corrective direction

chunks.summary:
The candidate should not enter interviews as a generic Unity developer, generic 3D artist or generalist full-stack developer.

The most defensible interview frame is:

> Real-Time 3D Developer / Unity Technical Artist focused on interactive technical visualization, CAD-to-realtime optimization, WebGL deployment and technical UI systems.

### Defensible claims

- Built a Unity WebGL interactive 3D technical visualization prototype for drone assembly understanding.
- Worked across CAD-to-realtime optimization, Unity integration, interaction systems, UI, visual modes and technical documentation.
- Used academic usability and workload metrics to evaluate the tool.
- Can explain asset optimization trade-offs, interaction design, WebGL constraints and validation methodology.
- Used AI as an implementation assistant while retaining technical judgment, debugging, integration and final ownership.

### Claims to avoid

locator.section: 13 — Interview, Negotiation and Offer-Risk Framework > 6. Technical question bank (parte 1/3)

chunks.summary:
This section is not intended for memorization. It defines categories that should be practiced with precise answers.

### Unity fundamentals

- What is a GameObject and how do components relate to it?
- Explain the Unity lifecycle: `Awake`, `Start`, `Update`, `FixedUpdate`, `LateUpdate`.
- When should `FixedUpdate` be used?
- What is a prefab and why does it matter in production?
- What are colliders and rigidbodies?
- How does Unity serialization work at a basic level?
- How do ScriptableObjects differ from MonoBehaviours?
- How would you structure object selection and highlighting?

### Performance and optimization

- How do you diagnose low FPS in Unity?
- What metrics do you check first: CPU, GPU, draw calls, batches, memory, textures, triangles?
- How would you optimize a CAD-imported scene?
- What is the difference between static batching, dynamic batching, GPU instancing and SRP batching?
- When should you use LODs?
- How do texture size and material count affect WebGL performance?
- What causes long load times in a browser build?
- How do you reduce memory pressure in Unity WebGL?

### Rendering and technical art

- How would you optimize first-load experience?

locator.section: 13 — Interview, Negotiation and Offer-Risk Framework > 7. TwinSight interview narrative (parte 1/2)

chunks.summary:
### 60-second version

> TwinSight X500 is my thesis project: a Unity WebGL interactive 3D technical-visualization prototype for understanding the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone. The goal was to move beyond static 2D documentation and help users understand spatial relationships between components. I worked on the Unity integration, interaction systems, UI, visual modes, CAD-to-realtime optimization and evaluation documentation. The project reduced heavy CAD geometry into a realtime-ready asset and was evaluated with usability and workload instruments.

locator.section: 13 — Interview, Negotiation and Offer-Risk Framework > 8. Take-home test risk analysis (parte 1/2)

chunks.summary:
Take-home tests can be useful, but they carry unpaid-labor and scope-risk problems.

### Acceptable take-home test

| Criterion | Acceptable form |
|---|---|
| Scope | 2–4 hours maximum |
| Objective | Skill demonstration |
| Dataset | Toy or anonymized data |
| IP | Candidate retains portfolio rights if generic |
| Feedback | Some review or next step |
| Deadline | Reasonable, not overnight |

### Risky take-home test

| Risk | Signal |
|---|---|
| Free labor | Production-ready feature requested |
| Unbounded scope | “Spend as much time as needed” |
| IP capture | Company keeps all code with no compensation |
| No feedback | Auto-rejection after work |
| Vague evaluation | No criteria |
| Excessive urgency | 24-hour turnaround for complex task |

### Refusal or boundary script

Use a firm but neutral boundary:

> I’m comfortable completing a focused technical assessment. To keep it fair, I can spend up to 3–4 hours and provide a short README explaining decisions and trade-offs. If the task requires production-ready implementation beyond that scope, I’d prefer to treat it as a paid trial or reduce the deliverable.

locator.section: 13 — Interview, Negotiation and Offer-Risk Framework > 8. Take-home test risk analysis (parte 2/2)

chunks.summary:
### Paid-trial preference

For complex real company work:

> This looks close to a production task. I can do it as a paid trial with a defined scope, deliverables, IP terms and timeline.

locator.section: 13 — Interview, Negotiation and Offer-Risk Framework > 13. AI-assisted development disclosure (parte 1/2)

chunks.summary:
AI use is not automatically disqualifying. Poor disclosure is the risk.

### Bad disclosure

Avoid:

> I used AI to build the project.

This sounds like lack of ownership.

### Better disclosure

Use:

> I used AI as an implementation assistant for iteration, code generation support and debugging. I was responsible for architecture decisions, integration, testing, debugging, technical judgment and final behavior.

### When asked “How much did you build yourself?”

Answer structure:

1. State ownership.
2. Separate AI assistance from engineering responsibility.
3. Explain a concrete decision you made.
4. Mention debugging and validation.
5. Offer to walk through code or architecture.

Example:

> The project was AI-assisted, but I owned the system design, Unity integration, debugging, interaction behavior, asset workflow decisions and final validation. I used AI the way many developers use autocomplete, documentation search or pair-programming support: as an accelerator, not as a replacement for technical judgment. I can walk through the interaction architecture and explain the decisions behind the pipeline.

### Evidence needed

13 — Interview, Negotiation and Offer-Risk Framework > 15. Offer evaluation scorecard

chunks.summary:
Use this scoring model before accepting any offer.

### Core scoring table

| Category | Weight | Score 1–5 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Role fit | 20% |  |
| Compensation | 20% |  |
| Remote legality | 15% |  |
| Portfolio leverage | 15% |  |
| Contract safety | 15% |  |
| Growth potential | 10% |  |
| Lifestyle/time-zone fit | 5% |  |

### Decision interpretation

| Weighted result | Decision |
|---|---|
| 4.2–5.0 | strong accept / negotiate upward |
| 3.5–4.1 | viable if terms are clean |
| 3.0–3.4 | negotiate or use as bridge |
| 2.5–2.9 | accept only if urgent |
| below 2.5 | reject |

### Minimum acceptance gates

Do not accept if any of these fail:

- no written contract;
- payment terms unclear;
- work authorization impossible;
- unpaid production task required;
- non-compete blocks future technical art/Unity work broadly;
- IP terms prevent portfolio use entirely without justification;
- expected compensation below survival/runway needs.

locator.section: 17. “How would you debug low FPS in Unity WebGL?” > Answer

chunks.summary:
```text
I would start by separating whether the bottleneck is CPU, GPU, memory, loading or browser-specific overhead.

First, I would profile in Unity and then test the WebGL build in the browser because editor performance can be misleading. I would check draw calls, triangle count, material count, texture sizes, overdraw, scripts running per frame and garbage allocation.

For WebGL specifically, I would also check build size, memory configuration, compression, asset loading, shader complexity and browser console warnings.

Then I would apply fixes based on evidence: reduce geometry, combine or simplify materials, optimize textures, remove unnecessary update loops, avoid allocations, simplify shaders, use LODs where appropriate and reduce UI or rendering overhead.
```

locator.section: 18. “How would you structure an exploded view system?” > Answer

chunks.summary:
```text
I would treat exploded view as a controlled transformation system.

Each component or group needs an original position and an exploded target position. The system should store those transforms, interpolate between them, and preserve assembly relationships through grouping or hierarchy.

For a technical visualization project, I would avoid random outward movement. The exploded direction should communicate structure, so it should be based on assembly logic, axes, component groups or manually authored offsets.

I would also keep it reversible, expose a slider or state control, and ensure selection/highlighting still works in both assembled and exploded states.
```

---

locator.section: 19. “How would you implement component selection?” > Answer

chunks.summary:
```text
I would use colliders, raycasting and a mapping between scene objects and component metadata.

The selection system should not only identify a mesh. It should connect the selected object to a data model containing name, category, technical information, hierarchy, parent/child relationships and UI behavior.

I would also separate visual feedback from selection logic. That way highlighting, isolation, ghosting or UI updates can be changed without rewriting the selection core.
```

---

locator.section: 20. “How would you implement cross-section / clipping?” > Answer

chunks.summary:
```text
At a high level, I would use a clipping plane or shader-based clipping approach, depending on the rendering pipeline and platform constraints.

The system needs a plane position, orientation and user control. Materials or shaders then discard fragments on one side of the plane. For Unity WebGL, I would keep the shader approach as simple as possible and test compatibility carefully.

If the project requires capped cross-sections or engineering-grade sectioning, that becomes more complex and may require mesh processing or specialized rendering techniques. For a visualization prototype, shader-based clipping is often a practical starting point.
```

locator.section: 21. “What is CAD-to-realtime?” > Answer

chunks.summary:
```text
CAD-to-realtime is the process of converting CAD or engineering-derived geometry into assets that can run efficiently in a real-time engine like Unity.

CAD models are usually built for precision and manufacturing, not for real-time rendering. They can contain dense geometry, excessive detail, problematic topology, many small parts, or structures that are inefficient for WebGL or real-time engines.

The workflow usually involves conversion, cleanup, simplification, retopology where needed, UV preparation, material planning, hierarchy organization, optimization and engine integration.

The goal is to preserve the technical meaning of the object while making it usable in an interactive real-time environment.
```

locator.section: 39. “Describe a time you solved a difficult problem” > Answer using TwinSight

chunks.summary:
```text
A difficult problem in TwinSight was converting dense CAD-derived geometry into assets suitable for real-time WebGL inspection.

The raw assets were not designed for browser-based rendering. They had to preserve enough detail to remain technically meaningful, but also be simplified enough to support interaction.

I approached it by analyzing the geometry, identifying what detail was necessary for recognition and assembly understanding, simplifying or rebuilding parts where needed, preparing assets in Blender and integrating them into Unity.

The result was an optimized model that preserved the inspection value of the assembly while becoming more appropriate for real-time visualization.
```

```text
no media

no license boundary
```

The current sample shows a viable but narrow path. Generic Unity roles skew toward senior game development, mobile, and shipped-title experience. The best fit for Alexander is not a generic game programmer lane; it is a technical visualization / technical art lane where Unity, C#, shaders, WebGL, optimization, Blender, and interactive 3D systems combine into one portfolio narrative.

The LATAM nearshore market is relevant, but small in this capture. The highest-value next step is not broad application volume. It is building a portfolio package that can satisfy the explicit expectations visible in Creamos, Mudtek, Flat2VR, Insight Global, and HyperVR: Unity proof, C# proof, optimization proof, visual proof, and project documentation.

locator.section: 4. 2-minute project explanation > Answer (parte 1/2)

chunks.summary:
```text
TwinSight X500 is a Unity WebGL technical visualization prototype for inspecting the assembly of a Holybro X500 V2 drone.

The problem was that static 2D assembly documentation forces users to mentally reconstruct spatial relationships between components, orientations and hidden structures. I wanted to test whether an interactive 3D viewer could support understanding more directly.

Technically, the project involved transforming CAD-derived drone geometry into an optimized real-time WebGL asset, organizing components for selection, implementing runtime interaction systems in Unity/C#, building technical UI panels with UI Toolkit, and adding features like exploded view, clipping/cross-section inspection and multiple visual modes.

The project was also evaluated as an academic prototype using SUS, NASA-TLX Raw and Think-Aloud methods. The formative results suggested high perceived usability and lower perceived workload for the 3D viewer condition compared with 2D support in the tested tasks.

locator.section: 4. 2-minute project explanation > Answer (parte 2/2)

chunks.summary:
For me, the value of the project is that it demonstrates the full pipeline: CAD-to-realtime optimization, Unity WebGL, runtime interaction, technical UI, technical visualization and evaluation.
```

locator.section: 5. Project defense: TwinSight questions > 5.1 What problem were you solving?

chunks.summary:
```text
The core problem was spatial understanding. Drone assembly documentation is often shown through 2D diagrams, part lists and written instructions. Users must mentally reconstruct how components relate in 3D space. TwinSight addresses that by turning the drone assembly into an interactive 3D viewer where users can select parts, see hierarchy through exploded view, cut through geometry and inspect technical information directly in context.
```

locator.section: 5. Project defense: TwinSight questions > 5.2 Why Unity WebGL?

chunks.summary:
```text
Unity gave me a mature real-time 3D environment for interaction systems, visual modes, UI and asset organization. WebGL was important because the prototype needed to run in the browser without requiring a local install. That made it more accessible for evaluation and more aligned with technical visualization tools that need to be shared easily.
```

locator.section: 5. Project defense: TwinSight questions > 5.3 Why not Three.js?

chunks.summary:
```text
Three.js would also be valid for browser-based 3D. I chose Unity WebGL because my project needed a real-time engine workflow with scene hierarchy, interaction systems, UI Toolkit, rendering modes and a pipeline closer to Unity technical-art and real-time visualization roles. For this portfolio direction, Unity was the stronger strategic fit.
```

locator.section: 5. Project defense: TwinSight questions > 5.4 Is it a digital twin?

chunks.summary:
```text
I would describe it as digital-twin-adjacent, not a full production digital twin. It represents a real physical drone assembly in interactive 3D, but it does not currently include live sensor data, operational state synchronization, predictive maintenance or real-time telemetry. The current scope is technical visualization and assembly inspection.
```

locator.section: 5. Project defense: TwinSight questions > 5.5 Is it a simulation?

chunks.summary:
```text
It is not a physics simulation. It is an interactive technical visualization prototype. It simulates inspection workflows visually, but it does not simulate drone physics, structural loads, heat transfer or flight behavior.
```

locator.section: 5. Project defense: TwinSight questions > 5.6 What was the hardest technical part?

chunks.summary:
```text
The hardest part was balancing technical readability with WebGL constraints. CAD-derived geometry can be too heavy for browser deployment, so the challenge was preserving enough visual detail for inspection while reducing geometry and organizing the model into selectable components. The second challenge was coordinating multiple runtime states: selection, exploded view, clipping, visual modes and UI panels.
```

locator.section: 5. Project defense: TwinSight questions > 5.7 What would you improve next?

chunks.summary:
```text
I would improve three areas. First, I would deepen the metadata system so each component has richer technical information. Second, I would add guided assembly steps and search/filter tools. Third, I would explore WebGPU, XR inspection or sensor-state integration as future extensions, while keeping the current version honest as a WebGL technical visualization prototype.
```

---

locator.section: 6. CAD-to-realtime optimization defense > 6.1 Explain the CAD pipeline

chunks.summary:
```text
The project started from CAD-derived geometry that was not suitable for direct real-time use. I inspected different conversion/tessellation routes, cleaned and optimized the assets in Blender, organized the model into logical components and prepared the geometry for Unity WebGL. The goal was not to preserve every CAD detail, but to preserve the visual information needed for assembly inspection while making the model usable in a browser.
```

locator.section: 6. CAD-to-realtime optimization defense > 6.2 Explain the triangle reduction

chunks.summary:
```text
The source routes exceeded 6.5M triangles in some forms, while the optimized runtime model was reduced to 95,617 triangles. I treat that as a portfolio and academic-prototype optimization metric, not as a production benchmark. The main point is that I could transform heavy CAD-derived data into a WebGL-ready inspection model while preserving component readability.
```

locator.section: 6. CAD-to-realtime optimization defense > 6.3 What did you decide to keep or remove?

chunks.summary:
```text
I prioritized silhouette, component identity, assembly relationships and features needed for inspection. I removed or simplified geometry that did not contribute to understanding the assembly, especially excessive tessellation or internal details that would not be visible or useful in the final viewer.
```

locator.section: 6. CAD-to-realtime optimization defense > 6.4 How did you handle fasteners?

chunks.summary:
```text
Fasteners were treated as modular repeated elements where possible. The goal was to avoid treating every screw as a unique asset when repeated geometry could be handled more efficiently. For a future production version, I would further standardize fastener families, metadata and instancing.
```

locator.section: 6. CAD-to-realtime optimization defense > 6.5 What would you do differently in a production pipeline?

chunks.summary:
```text
In production I would formalize the optimization pipeline more strictly: asset naming rules, automated validation, LOD strategy, texture budgets, profiler targets, versioned exports, and clearer handoff between CAD, DCC tools and Unity. I would also define target device constraints earlier.
```

locator.section: 7. Unity / C# technical screen defense > 7.2 Explain selection system

chunks.summary:
```text
The selection system connects user input to selectable drone components. When a part is selected, the viewer updates highlighting and displays contextual technical information in the UI. The important design point is separating the selectable component identity from the visual feedback and metadata presentation.
```

locator.section: 7. Unity / C# technical screen defense > 7.3 Explain exploded view

chunks.summary:
```text
The exploded view is a state-based transformation of assembly components. Instead of random separation, each component or group needs a defined offset direction and target position so the assembly remains understandable. The value is preserving spatial logic while making component relationships visible.
```

locator.section: 7. Unity / C# technical screen defense > 7.4 Explain clipping

chunks.summary:
```text
The clipping tool allows the user to cut through the model visually to inspect hidden structures. In Unity this can be handled through shader/material logic or clipping plane approaches depending on the implementation. The goal is not destructive geometry editing, but runtime visual inspection.
```

locator.section: 7. Unity / C# technical screen defense > 7.5 Explain visual modes

chunks.summary:
```text
The visual modes are inspection states that change how the model is rendered or interpreted visually. Some modes support readability, like realistic and solid modes. Others expose structure, like X-ray, ghosted, blueprint or wireframe modes. The thermal-style mode is qualitative only; it is not a physical simulation.
```

locator.section: 7. Unity / C# technical screen defense > 7.6 Explain UI Toolkit usage

chunks.summary:
```text
UI Toolkit was used to structure technical panels and interaction controls in a way that could support a more app-like interface. The interface needed to display component data while keeping the 3D inspection workflow visible.
```

locator.section: 7. Unity / C# technical screen defense > 7.7 Possible technical questions

chunks.summary:
| Question | Answer direction |
|---|---|
| How do you avoid coupling UI and model logic? | separate component metadata, selection state and UI rendering |
| How do you optimize for WebGL? | geometry reduction, texture budget, draw calls, loading, UI simplicity |
| How do you manage visual modes? | central mode manager, materials/shaders/states |
| How do you debug WebGL builds? | browser console, Unity logs, simplified repro scenes |
| How do you handle large models? | split hierarchy, optimize mesh, instancing, LOD, compression |
| How do you scale to multiple products? | metadata schema, import pipeline, prefab conventions |
